notes:
• Aim: smoother, steadier aim. A new page that finds what makes your aim feel rough on your PC (your mouse, uneven frames, a screen that can't follow them, freezes from other apps) and how to fix each. Your sensitivity in real numbers (cm per 360°, the same feel in other games), a 3-minute finder that measures the sensitivity your hand tracks and flicks best with, and a curve that's slow for tracking and quick for big turns, set through Raw Accel and put back any time.
  • Fans that keep your graphics card cool while you play. A new Fans page: pick Quiet, Balanced or Cool, or drag the curve yourself, and choose your highest speed. TEMPO never goes past 90% and warns above 80%, and the fans go back to normal the moment the game closes, even after a crash.
  • Play checks first. Pressing Play looks at what could cost this match (memory, an app that froze your last games, downloads, the game's drive, Steam launch options, no fps limit), fixes what it can in one click, then opens the game.
  • After every match, a card that tells you how it went against your usual for that game: average, worst moments, how smooth it was, stutters, heat, and the one thing that held it back, with what to do about it.
  • Every match, minute by minute. Point at a session's chart for that moment's fps, dips, heat, fan speed and any stutter.
  • It names the app that froze your game. When a long stutter lines up with another app suddenly grabbing the processor (NVIDIA's app, MSI Afterburner, Discord, a browser...), TEMPO says which one and what to change in it.
  • Game settings reach the game, on any PC. TEMPO now finds the settings file each game really uses: the copy your Steam account uses (Deadlock, Counter-Strike 2), the right folder for Unreal Engine games, and Minecraft from any launcher (CurseForge, Prism, Modrinth and more). The Tune page shows where the file is and whether the game itself saved it during a match. Changes that went to an old copy before are offered again.
  • Frame delay, measured: how long from the game starting a frame to it reaching your screen, live and on every match card.
  • Mouse check on the Checkup page: your mouse's real polling rate, how evenly its reports arrive, and the settings around it that change how aim feels.
  • NVIDIA driver profile for any game: an fps limit that works even in games without one, low latency mode and power management.
  • Pause apps while you play (off until you switch it on): browsers and Wallpaper Engine are paused, not closed, and their memory goes to the game. They wake the moment you switch to them, even if TEMPO crashes.
  • More games: GOG and Ubisoft Connect games in your list, and settings for Minecraft, Apex Legends, Schedule I and more of Counter-Strike 2.
  • A new look: a short intro when TEMPO opens, softer cards, an icon for every setting, new switches and sliders, smoother charts, glass panels, a dark tray menu, and the same roomy layout on 125% and 150% displays.
  • On your desktop in one click. The first time TEMPO opens it offers a desktop and Start menu shortcut (also on the Look page). Opened straight from the zip, it first copies itself somewhere lasting, and the shortcuts follow TEMPO to newer versions.
  • Fps limit advice from the match itself, never under 60. Smooth windowed mode for older DirectX games. The overlay says when it costs a frame of delay. Know your PC: the exact memory stick to add, a screen plugged into the motherboard, a graphics card on half its lanes.
  • On a PC whose graphics card doesn't let apps set its fans (AMD and Intel cards, most laptops), the Fans tab is greyed out and says why.

Everything from 1.3 stays: the boost, Tune and its tests, sessions, the overlay, the phone view, Look.

notes:
• Repair internet settings (Settings, "If browsers lose the internet"): puts Windows' proxy setting back to normal. Older LinkFuse versions could leave it pointing at LinkFuse after a crash, or if LinkFuse was deleted while fused, and then browsers had no internet. A proxy of your own is kept. Also from the command line: LinkFuse.exe --repair.
  • LinkFuse now fixes such a leftover by itself when it opens.
  • Windows' proxy setting is now changed through Windows' own settings API, so every copy Windows keeps of it stays in step (before, the registry values were written directly and Windows' saved copy could keep an old address).
  • Fix: turning Proxy mode on while an older version's leftover was still set could back up that leftover as your setting and put it back later. Backups never hold LinkFuse's own addresses any more.

Unzip over the old folder and open LinkFuse.exe. Your settings carry over.

summary: Apps step back by themselves. TEMPO knows browsers, launchers, cloud sync, updaters, RGB and wallpaper apps, and steps back anything else that keeps…

An app you switch to gets its full speed while it's in front.
notes:
Everything from 1.3, plus a polish pass:

  • Apps step back by themselves. TEMPO knows browsers, launchers, cloud sync, updaters, RGB and wallpaper apps, and steps back anything else that keeps the processor busy while you play. Tap any app to decide for yourself, or switch to "I pick".
  • Kept as they are: calls and music, and everything your game needs: anti-cheat, frame generation like Lossless Scaling, overlays, recording, mouse and controller software (including Steam), VPNs and fan tools. Nothing of the game itself ever steps back.
  • An app you switch to gets its full speed while it's in front.
  • Launchers and restarts: a launcher handing over to the game is followed, and TEMPO waits 20 seconds after the game closes before turning off.
  • Steam launch options explained on the Tune page, and suggestions put fixes and fps gains first.
  • Turning on and off has its own moment, and a session receipt rises with your numbers when a game ends.
  • Apps are shown by the names you know (Epic Games, Wallpaper Engine, Phone Link), easier-to-read text, and a short "what's new" after an update.
  • Checkup warns about Steam launch options like -high and -fullscreen for the game you picked.
  • If another app already uses Ctrl Alt T or Ctrl Alt O, TEMPO says so instead of failing quietly.
  • Sessions from the very first TEMPO show their stutters as "not counted" instead of 0, and tips only name apps that really step back.

summary: Tune: a new page that finds what actually helps this game on this PC.
Tests: "Test it" switches a setting on and off between your sessions and measures both, at least three sessions each.
The game's own settings: Deadlock, Counter-Strike 2, Unreal Engine games and Unity games (window mode).
notes:
• Tune: a new page that finds what actually helps this game on this PC. After one normal session it suggests changes made for your PC. Nothing changes unless you press a button.
  • Tests: "Test it" switches a setting on and off between your sessions and measures both, at least three sessions each. TEMPO only says better or worse when the difference is clearly bigger than the usual ups and downs between matches. Each part of the boost can be tested the same way.
  • The game's own settings: Deadlock, Counter-Strike 2, Unreal Engine games and Unity games (window mode). Only while the game is closed, only settings already in the file, with a backup first, and a "Put back" button for every change.
  • Fps limit advice: the limit your PC can hold most of the time, for evenly spaced frames.
  • What caused each stutter: memory, heat, another app, loading, the processor slowing down, or the game itself.
  • Free memory when it runs short, and game on the strong graphics card on PCs with two graphics chips.
  • On your phone: live fps, heat and stutters over your home Wi-Fi by scanning a QR code, even in exclusive fullscreen. Off until you switch it on.

TEMPO 1.0.0, game performance, measured properly.

Pick a game, turn TEMPO on, open the game. While it's on, TEMPO boosts your PC for the game, shows your fps on top of it, and saves a report when you're done: your average, the dips you feel, and what held your fps back. Turn it off and everything goes back.

  • The boost: the apps you pick step back (lower priority and Windows' efficiency mode, never closed), your game gets the processor first, Windows Game Mode on, Game Bar background recording paused, high performance power. Music and voice apps (Discord, Spotify and more) are never touched.
  • Everything is undone when TEMPO turns off, and after a crash the next start puts it all back first.
  • Your own fps counter: three styles, any corner, as see-through as you like.
  • Reports with 1% and 0.1% lows, what limited your fps, background apps, heat, and boost against no boost.
  • Nothing is injected into games: TEMPO reads Windows' own frame timing (built on Intel PresentMon, MIT).
